reports.title: Meta Launches Muse Wonder, Its First Frontier AI Model: Can It Pay for the Capex?

editorial.summary:
Meta has released Muse Wonder, which outlets describe as its first frontier AI model family, according to The Daily Star, ExtremeTech and AI Insider. AI Insider reported that the models come from Meta Superintelligence Lab and mark the company's first push into frontier AI. Intelligent Living referred to two versions, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full.

Konsulteer reported that the models feature long-term memory and advanced coding capabilities. Technology Org reported a price of $4 per million tokens. ExtremeTech framed the launch as Meta taking on Anthropic and OpenAI, while TIKR.com raised the question of whether the release can pay for Meta's capital spending. Fortune also examined what Muse Wonder and frontier AI mean for Meta.
editorial.whyItMatters: Meta's entry with its own frontier models adds another large lab to the race with OpenAI and Anthropic, and ties that competition to the heavy infrastructure spending needed to sustain it.
keyFacts: Meta Superintelligence Lab released Muse Wonder, its first frontier AI models, according to AI Insider.
Intelligent Living named two versions: Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full.
Konsulteer reported long-term memory and advanced coding features.
Technology Org reported pricing of $4 per million tokens.
editorial.note: The Yahoo Finance report concerns Anthropic reaching a milestone and the CNET report concerns Google's Gemini 4 Argon, so they cover different events than Meta's Muse Wonder.

replacement.reason: A new frontier model release with coding and memory features raises capability, modestly pushing toward automating work, but no direct job impact is reported.

extinction.reason: A competing frontier model launch adds to industry race dynamics, but reports cite no safety testing, weapons uplift, or loss-of-control concerns.

A Guide to Which AI CEOs Now Say ‘Super Intelligence’ and Which Don’t

editorial.summary:
Gizmodo published a guide tracking which AI company chief executives now use the term "superintelligence" in their public remarks and which avoid it. Other outlets covered the term from different angles. UA.NEWS, citing Deutsche Welle, reported that Trump announced the creation of a Super Intelligence Force in the US. Egypt Independent asked whether Trump's push to make "super intelligence" happen would succeed, and The Jerusalem Strategic Tribune described Washington as redefining the rules around superintelligence. Fast Company South Africa framed a debate over whether the field is artificial intelligence or super intelligence.

CRN carried an interview with Arctic Wolf CEO Nick Schneider on frontier AI guardrails, in which he said that right now frontier AI developers do not have guardrails figured out. A NASA page titled "Super Intelligence" was also among the reports listed for this event.
editorial.whyItMatters: The coverage shows that the word "superintelligence" has become a point of contention among AI leaders and government officials, with differing views on its meaning and use. For AI safety discussions, Schneider's remarks add a view on the state of guardrails for frontier systems.
keyFacts: Gizmodo's guide sorts AI CEOs by whether they say "superintelligence" publicly.
According to UA.NEWS, citing Deutsche Welle, Trump announced the creation of a Super Intelligence Force in the US.
CRN quoted Arctic Wolf CEO Nick Schneider saying frontier AI developers do not yet have guardrails figured out.
editorial.note: The NASA item carries only the title "Super Intelligence" and does not describe the same event as the other reports, so it is not treated as corroborating them.

extinction.reason: Mainly terminology coverage; the CEO remark that developers lack guardrails is a mild warning with no concrete new evidence.

Super Intelligence: Washington Redefines the Rules

Super Intelligence
Which Tech Leaders Are Adopting Trump’s ‘Super Intelligence’ Rebrand?

editorial.summary:
According to Firstpost, the Trump administration rolled out SI.gov as part of a push to rebrand artificial intelligence as "super intelligence." Deutsche Welle, as cited by UA.NEWS, reported that Trump announced the creation of a Super Intelligence Force in the United States.

Politico reported that Kupor said a "Super Intelligence" task force would press companies on AI safety. Tech-insider.org reported that searches for "super intelligence" had tripled, while Newsweek asked which tech leaders are adopting the rebrand.
editorial.whyItMatters: The reports tie the term to a government body that would press AI companies on safety, which bears directly on how frontier developers may be overseen. Whether the rebrand gains industry uptake will matter for how the policy is understood.
keyFacts: Firstpost reported the administration rolled out SI.gov as part of a push to rebrand AI as super intelligence.
Deutsche Welle, cited by UA.NEWS, reported that Trump announced a Super Intelligence Force.
Politico reported that Kupor said the Super Intelligence task force will press companies on AI safety.
Tech-insider.org reported that searches for "super intelligence" had tripled.
editorial.note: Reports differ on whether the initiative is a Super Intelligence Force, a SI.gov rollout, or a task force, and a NASA.gov page with the same title does not appear to concern the same initiative.

extinction.reason: A government task force reportedly pressing companies on AI safety is a mild oversight signal, but the reports give few details.
